stem:
Hemant knows the number of taps and the time to fill a fixed tank are inversely proportional. With $5$ taps the job takes $12$ hours. He needs the time when $8$ taps work on the same tank.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Keep the product constant: $5\times12=8\times t$, so $t=\dfrac{60}{8}=7.5$ hours.
The constant product is only a label, so ignore the fixed tank and pick any time.
Scale time the same way as taps: $t=12\times\dfrac{8}{5}=19.2$ hours, as if the tank size need not stay fixed.
The answer is $12$ hours because $12$ is the only time printed in the stem.

teacher.key_rationale: Inverse proportion keeps the product fixed for the same tank: 5×12=8×t gives t=7.5 h. Treating 'constant product' as a mere label swaps the hinge. Direct scaling omits the fixed-tank condition. Reusing the printed 12 is a surface grab.
